name: Shopify

composio.note: Bring your own app. Composio has no managed Shopify app, so you create one in the Shopify Dev Dashboard and paste its client ID and secret into a Composio auth config. Each connection is for one store: the user gives the store subdomain (e.g. `your-store`, not the full host) and installs your app on that store.

verdict.headline: Connecting your own dev store takes an afternoon; letting any merchant connect means public distribution and Shopify App Store review, which takes weeks and needs a production-ready app.
verdict.summary: Apps are now created in the Dev Dashboard (dev.shopify.com). You pick a distribution method once and cannot change it: custom distribution installs on one store or one Plus organization with no review, public distribution needs App Store review. Customer name, email, phone and address are protected customer data and need a separate Level 2 access request and review for public apps. OAuth is per shop, new public apps must use expiring offline tokens, and public apps must handle three mandatory compliance webhooks.

toProduction.label: Custom distribution: same day per merchant. Public distribution: about 2–8 weeks

activeEffort.label: 2–4 hours (custom); 20–80 hours (public, incl. review prep, webhooks, data protection details)

approval.name: Shopify App Store review (public distribution) + protected customer data access review
approval.trigger: Public distribution always needs App Store review. Reading customer name, email, phone or address on non-development stores needs a protected customer data request; public apps are reviewed for both Level 1 and Level 2. Some scopes (e.g. read_all_orders for Partner-org apps, read_users, taxes, payment scopes) need separate approval. Custom distribution needs no review.
approval.wait: Not documented. Community reports suggest roughly 1–4 weeks per review round, longer with resubmissions (inferred).

prerequisites.text: A Shopify developer account with access to the Dev Dashboard (dev.shopify.com). Use a Partner organization if you plan public distribution; distribution choice only appears for Partner-org apps.
A development store to test on. Apps installed only on development stores can read protected customer data without a review request.
For public distribution: App Store registration (one-time fee), a production-ready app, a screencast, and test credentials/instructions for reviewers.
A Composio account to create the auth config.

oauth.refreshTokens: Offline tokens are not tied to a staff member. New public apps must request expiring offline tokens (`expiring=1`): access token ~1 hour (`expires_in` 3600), refresh token 90 days (`refresh_token_expires_in` 7776000), refreshed with `grant_type=refresh_token`. Online tokens (`grant_options[]=per-user`) expire with the user session and have no refresh token. Client-credentials tokens (own-org stores only) last 24 hours.
oauth.redirectUriRules: Must exactly match a redirect URL configured in the Dev Dashboard app version or the `[auth]` section of `shopify.app.toml`. Validate `hmac`, `state`, and the `shop` param (`^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9\-]*\.myshopify\.com$`) on callback.

steps.title: Open the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Go to dev.shopify.com. App creation moved here from the Partner Dashboard. From a store admin you can also search **App development** and choose **Build apps in Dev Dashboard**.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Create a new app in the Dev Dashboard (fine for API-only apps) or with Shopify CLI. Set the **App URL**.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config and copy its redirect URI
steps.detail: In the Composio dashboard: **Create Auth Config** → Shopify → **OAuth2** → use your own developer credentials. Copy the redirect URI the dashboard shows. Composio's Shopify page shows `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback`; Composio's generic guides show `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` (not confirmed for Shopify). The dashboard value is authoritative.

steps.title: Set scopes and redirect URL, then release a version
steps.detail: In the app version, pick only the scopes you need (e.g. `read_products`, `read_orders`). Add the Composio redirect URL exactly. Click **Release**; config changes apply only to released versions. Do not declare scopes marked "Shopify approval required" yet, or the version fails with an `app_access` error.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Dev Dashboard → app → **Settings** → copy Client ID and Client Secret. Paste them into the Composio auth config and save. You get an auth config ID starting with `ac_`.

steps.title: Connect your development store
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection with the store **subdomain** only (`your-store`). Composio sends you to `https://your-store.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize`; approve the install. An agent can drive this once a human approves in the browser.

steps.title: Verify API calls
steps.detail: Run a read tool (e.g. `SHOPIFY_GRAPH_QL_QUERY` or `SHOPIFY_GET_ORDERS_WITH_FILTERS`). If customer fields come back `null`, you need protected customer data access (select the fields in the dashboard; dev-store-only apps need no review).

steps.title: Choose distribution (one-way decision)
steps.detail:
App **Home** → **Distribution** card → **Select distribution method**. It cannot be changed later.
- **Custom**: one store, or several stores in one Plus org. No review. Cannot use Shopify app billing.
- **Public**: any merchant. Requires App Store review.
If you keep separate dev and prod apps, choose on the prod app.

steps.title: Custom path: send install link to the merchant
steps.detail: Enter the merchant's `myshopify.com` domain, click **Generate link**, and send it. The merchant installs the app; then they connect through Composio with their subdomain. Repeat per merchant (one app per store/Plus org).

steps.title: Public path: request protected customer data access
steps.detail: If you read customer name, email, phone or address: **API access requests** → **Protected customer data access** → select data and fields with reasons → fill **Data protection details**. Level 2 needs encrypted backups, access logs, incident response policy and more.

steps.title: Public path: implement compliance webhooks and expiring tokens
steps.detail: Subscribe to `customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact`; verify HMAC (return `401` if invalid), return 2xx, act within 30 days. Composio does not host these for you, so you need your own endpoint (inferred). New public apps must use expiring offline tokens.

steps.title: Public path: submit for App Store review
steps.detail: Register for the App Store (one-time fee), complete the listing, include a screencast and test credentials, and submit. Statuses: Draft → Submitted → Reviewed/Paused → Published. Reply to reviewer emails to keep it moving.

steps.title: Wait for review
steps.detail: Shopify assigns a reviewer. No official timeline is published. Each resubmission restarts part of the wait.

steps.title: Each merchant installs and connects
steps.detail: Even after approval, each merchant installs the app on their own store and authorizes it. Connections are per store.

scopes.name: read_products / write_products
scopes.purpose: Products and variants. Write implies read.

scopes.name: read_orders / write_orders
scopes.purpose: Orders from the last 60 days only.

scopes.name: read_all_orders
scopes.purpose: Orders older than 60 days. Use with read_orders. Partner-org apps must request it under API access requests; merchant-org apps don't.

scopes.name: read_customers / write_customers
scopes.purpose: Customer records. Name, email, phone and address fields are protected customer data (Level 2) and return null without approval on non-dev stores.

scopes.name: read_users
scopes.purpose: Staff members. Shopify Plus only; needs Shopify approval.

scopes.name: read_taxes / write_taxes, payment and subscription scopes
scopes.purpose: Need Shopify approval before you can declare them.

gotchas.title: Distribution method is permanent
gotchas.detail: Once you pick custom or public, you can't switch. A custom app only installs on one store or one Plus org. If you might go public, create a separate prod app and choose public there.

gotchas.title: Customer PII comes back null, not as an error
gotchas.detail: Without protected customer data approval, GraphQL returns HTTP 200 with redacted fields (e.g. `"phone": null`) and an error in `errors`. It works on dev stores and then silently breaks on real stores. Request Level 2 access early; for public apps it is reviewed.

gotchas.title: Orders older than 60 days are invisible
gotchas.detail: `read_orders` only covers 60 days. `read_all_orders` needs a request for Partner-org apps. Composio reports 403s on order reads without it.

gotchas.title: Public review expects a production-ready app, not just an OAuth client
gotchas.detail: Reviewers need a working install flow, a UI to review, a screencast and test credentials. A pure backend connector for an agent may struggle to pass; plan the App URL and merchant-facing UX (inferred from the review criteria).

gotchas.title: Compliance webhooks are on you
gotchas.detail: Public apps must subscribe to `customers/data_request`, `customers/redact` and `shop/redact` even if they store no personal data. Composio's hosted flow doesn't cover these; you need your own HTTPS endpoint.

gotchas.title: Managed installation is for CLI apps, not Composio
gotchas.detail: Shopify CLI apps default to managed installation and token exchange, with scopes in `shopify.app.toml`. Composio connects through the authorization code grant at `/admin/oauth/authorize`, so keep the redirect URL registered and treat the CLI template flow as separate. Adding scopes later means merchants must re-authorize (inferred for the Composio flow).

gotchas.title: Expiring offline tokens for new public apps
gotchas.detail: New public apps must use expiring offline tokens: 1-hour access token, 90-day refresh token. A connection idle for 90+ days needs re-auth. Composio says it handles refresh; whether it sends `expiring=1` was not confirmed.

gotchas.title: Use subdomain only in Composio
gotchas.detail: Pass `your-store`, not `your-store.myshopify.com`. Composio builds the host.

gotchas.title: Own-org stores can skip OAuth
gotchas.detail: If the app and store are in the same organization, Shopify recommends the client credentials grant (24-hour tokens). Composio also offers an S2S option. This is not a path for other merchants' stores.

blockers.symptom: OAuth 400 during token exchange or connection start
blockers.fix: Re-enter the client secret in the Composio auth config, confirm requested scopes are approved for the app, then start a fresh connection.

blockers.symptom: Redirect URI error on the Shopify authorize page
blockers.fix: Copy the exact callback from the Composio dashboard into the app's redirect URLs and release a new version. It must match exactly.

blockers.symptom: App version fails to release with an `app_access` error on `scopes`
blockers.fix: Remove the "Shopify approval required" scope, request approval (Support or API access requests), then add it back.

blockers.symptom: "This app is not approved to access the Customer object" / customer fields null
blockers.fix: Request protected customer data access and the specific fields; public apps must pass the data protection review.

blockers.symptom: Merchant can't install: app can only be installed on stores in the same organization
blockers.fix: Generate a custom distribution install link for that store, or use public distribution. Community reports say collaborator access isn't enough (inferred).

blockers.symptom: App Store review paused or rejected: no redirect to OAuth screen, fatal error after install, failed re-install, missing test credentials, unfinished app
blockers.fix: Fix the install flow and re-install handling, add a screencast and test credentials, then resubmit. Resubmissions slow the review.

objects.name: Orders
objects.description: Orders with line items, transactions and fulfillments.
objects.note: read_orders only covers orders from the last 60 days. Older orders need read_all_orders, which Partner apps must request and get approved. Orders count as protected customer data, so public apps need protected data review, and name, email, phone and address return null until those fields are approved.

objects.name: Products and variants
objects.description: Products, variants, collections and selling plans.

objects.name: Customers
objects.description: Customer records, segments and B2B companies.
objects.note: Protected customer data. Public apps need Level 1 approval for customer data and Level 2 approval for name, email, phone and address. Unapproved fields return null with a GraphQL error, still with HTTP 200. Custom apps and development stores do not need review.

objects.name: Inventory
objects.description: Inventory items and stock levels per location.

objects.name: Fulfillments
objects.description: Fulfillments on orders and fulfillment orders.
objects.note: Fulfillments on orders come with read_orders. The access scopes page says some fulfillment-order scopes need Shopify approval, so check the scope list before you request them.

objects.name: Draft orders
objects.description: Draft orders created by staff or apps.
objects.note: Draft orders can hold customer details, so protected customer data rules likely apply to those fields.

changes.detail: Subscribe per topic to an HTTPS URL, a Google Pub/Sub topic or an Amazon EventBridge source. Verify the X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header. Respond within 5 seconds. Failed deliveries are retried up to 8 times over 4 hours, then the subscription is removed if failures persist. Order is not guaranteed and duplicates happen: dedupe on X-Shopify-Webhook-Id, sequence on updated_at, and run reconciliation jobs because delivery is not guaranteed. Public apps must also handle the customers/data_request, customers/redact and shop/redact compliance webhooks. Webhook payloads with customer data follow protected customer data rules. Composio-managed auth polls triggers at a 15-minute minimum; your own OAuth app can poll faster where the toolkit supports it.

limits.text: The GraphQL Admin API uses cost-based rate limits in a leaky bucket. Limits vary by plan. A single query cannot cost more than 1,000 points. On throttling, back off about one second.
Pagination is cursor-based with at most 250 items per page, and a connection can be paged through at most 25,000 objects.

For large syncs use bulk query operations. Results come as a JSONL file whose URL expires after one week. From API version 2026-01 an app can run up to 5 bulk queries per shop at once. An operation must finish within 10 days. Subscribe to bulk_operations/finish to know when it is done.
Without read_all_orders, order history stops at 60 days.

restrictions.text: The API terms bar using API or merchant data to train, fine-tune or improve AI or machine learning systems without Shopify's written consent or the merchant's consent for their own data.
Store or copy merchant data only as needed to serve that merchant, request only the minimum data needed, and do not sell or share it with third parties.
Delete merchant data within 30 days of uninstall or a valid deletion request. shop/redact arrives 48 hours after uninstall.
Level 2 protected customer data adds security duties such as encrypted backups, access logging and an incident response policy.
